response.summary: Two departments are currently flagged as over capacity: Operations and Maintenance.
concerns: Operations (12 headcount) logged 180 overtime hours last month, the highest of any department, consistent with its over-capacity status.
Maintenance (6 headcount) logged 96 overtime hours last month, also consistent with over-capacity status, and this is the smaller team so the strain per person may be more acute.

Both over-capacity departments have an open role: Maintenance Coordinator (approved, 63 days open - the longest open role) and Operations Associate (pending budget, 21 days open), suggesting hiring is already underway but not yet resolved.
response.recommendation: Prioritize finalizing the approved Maintenance Coordinator hire given it has been open 63 days, and escalate budget approval for the Operations Associate role since Operations is the largest team by overtime hours and headcount among the over-capacity departments. Consider reviewing whether overtime patterns in these two departments justify additional headcount beyond the currently open roles, though a skills/workload deep-dive would need data not held in this system.
missingInformation: No skills matrix exists, so it's not possible to say whether the over-capacity issue in operations/maintenance stems from specific skill gaps.
No salary or budget data is available in HR's authorised fields, so the cost implications of filling these roles cannot be assessed here (Finance-owned data).
No forward headcount forecast beyond the two currently open roles, so it's unclear if capacity pressure will persist or grow.
